description.value: This study investigated whether sub-acute naltrexone treatment and A118G genotype interacted in their effects on cue-elicited activation of the ventral striatum, medial prefrontal cortex, and orbitofrontal cortex.

spans.text: This study investigated whether sub-acute NTX treatment and A118G genotype interacted in their effects on cue-elicited activation of the ventral striatum (VS), medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC), and orbitofrontal cortex (OFC).

description.value: Seventy-four non-treatment-seeking alcohol-dependent individuals were randomized to naltrexone or placebo for 7 days and underwent an fMRI alcohol cue reactivity task on day 6.

spans.text: Seventy-four non-treatment-seeking alcohol-dependent individuals, half preselected to carry at least one copy of the A118G G (Asp) allele, were randomized to NTX (50 mg) or placebo for 7 days, and performed an fMRI alcohol cue reactivity task on day 6.
Subjects were then randomized, on the basis of their A118G genotype, to receive either NTX or matched placebo for 7 days.
Subjects were blind to their genotype group, and both subjects and investigators were blind to medication assignment.

A 720-second fMRI alcohol cue-reactivity task consisting of 24 pseudorandomly interspersed blocks of alcoholic beverage images, non-alcoholic beverage images, blurred visual controls, and fixation.

instructions.value: Subjects received a 10-ml sip of their preferred 80-proof liquor mixed with fruit juice before the task.

stimuli.value: Alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverage images, blurred versions of both, and a fixation cross; images were drawn from a normative appetitive picture set and advertisements.
